chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who has prayed two rak'ahs and does not know whether they are two or four. He said: He gives salām, then stands and prays two rak'ahs with Fatihat al-Kitab, then departs, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعٌ: Four rak'ahs, the alternative number being doubted.
key_terms.بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: With Surat al-Fatihah recited in the two compensatory rak'ahs.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two units of salat in this ruling of doubt.
key_terms.فَيُصَلِّي: He then performs the prescribed follow-up prayer.
key_terms.وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: No further obligation, penalty, or corrective burden remains upon him.
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: He concludes the prayer with salām.

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he doubts whether he has prayed two rak'ahs or four in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who doubts in salat whether he has prayed two rak'ahs or four. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs him to conclude the prayer, then stand and perform two additional rak'ahs with Fatihat al-Kitab, after which no further liability remains upon him.
